Consult Summary:
- Acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea and dehydration in a 48-year-old man with asthma; management includes oral rehydration, symptomatic treatment, and temporary work absence with planned follow-up if not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of acute diarrhea with prior vomiting; stools watery and loose; feverish sensation earlier; currently feeling weak and dehydrated.
- Onset, duration, progression:
  - Vomited a few times at onset (3 days ago) followed by onset of diarrhea.
  - Diarrhea started ~3 days ago; 5–6 bowel movements per day; stools are watery.
  - Vomiting has resolved; appetite is reduced; currently dehydrated feeling.
  - No persistent fever; previously felt warm but now generally feeling fine.
- Exacerbating, initiating, or relieving factors:
  - Drinking fluids is difficult because frequent toilet trips worsen dehydration; attempts to drink lead to further toilet use.
  - No clear dietary trigger identified; no takeaway/restaurant exposure recalled.
- Associated symptoms:
  - No significant abdominal pain reported.
  - No blood in stool.
  - General weakness; reduced oral intake.
  - No headaches or muscle pains reported.
- Systems review and negatives:
  - Temperature: previously warm, now not notably febrile.
  - No chest pain, dizziness, or syncope noted.
- Relevant past medical history: Asthma; uses blue inhaler (infrequently) for symptoms.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Medications: Inhaler (blue) used as needed; no other regular medications documented.
- Social history: Lives alone; employed as a software engineer; has taken the last three days off work due to illness; drinks alcohol socially/infrequently; does not smoke.
- Family history: Father had hypertension; died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; mother has type 2 diabetes.
- Occupation/functional status: Software engineer; off work for several days; currently not working due to illness.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration.
  - Plan:
    - Increase fluid intake; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replenish fluids and minerals.
    - Paracetamol as needed for fever or weakness.
    - Continue time off work for the next day or two until diarrhoea resolves; plan to return to work after being diarrhoea-free for 24–48 hours.
    - If not improved over the next week, return for re-evaluation.
- Issue 2: Asthma history.
  - Plan:
    - Continue blue inhaler (as-needed) for symptoms; advise monitoring for wheeze or shortness of breath and seeking care if symptoms worsen.

General plan:
- Monitor hydration status and symptom progression over the next several days.
- Follow up if not improving or if new symptoms (e.g., fever, abdominal pain, blood in stool, inability to keep fluids down) develop.
